The two adjacent concerns are bounded OUT with standing addresses: the interpreter's own staleness (discovered.py records it, measured 2026-08-13) and the beat overspend (CairnCommons/tickets/the-beat-spends-2500ms-on-triggers-against-a-1s-cadence.json... cast as named in MAP backlog).

questions.a: pulse.py is the SHIM's pulse (Akien's verbatim) — discovery changes where the roster comes from, never where firing lives; a loop that executes directly is the recorded 584aa74 goof and stays dead
class-level and instance-level pulses need no precedence rule: the unit is the FILE, each one found is one service at one address, both fire
identity is path+mtime, so an in-place edit is a remove+add in one beat — the freshest-commit-one-beat-away property holds for changed pulses, not only new ones

'the loop cannot go stale' is bounded to pulse-carried code: unload evicts the pulse module, not its transitively imported base modules; the resident interpreter's own staleness is measured prior art and OUT
run-vs-import decided v0: import, mtime-cached, matching probes/ — run-in-a-fresh-namespace is the recorded fallback if import accretion measures as a problem
questions/open-who-owns-the-ground-loops-restart resolves with this design: nobody — a correctly built loop has nothing to restart for

PROVED 2026-08-15: 11 teeth green twice under netns (seal at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/validations/test_pulse_service.json), verdict verdict-20260815T103426-9c2706a67f40 all 7 criteria pass, all 8 hypotheses confirmed

live fire at the resident singleton: one deployment restart (pid 3592949 -> 3933751), a dropped instance-level pulse served in 2.12s and a removed one unloaded in ~3s — one beat each at the MEASURED 3.65s cadence, same pid throughout; the cadence number itself feeds ticket the-beat-spends-2500ms-on-triggers-against-a-1s-cadence (worse than the 2.5s it was cast with)

the WATCHME probe measures its own beat-bound from the event stream (seconds-per-beat from two events on distinct beats) and labels the 10s fallback when it cannot — a coarse measurement to sharpen, never a hidden constant

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(a-dropped-pulse-serves-within-a-beat) -> PROVED -> [SUPERSEDED]

watchme.trigger: each read of the probe over the loop's own pulse-roster record (~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/0/) — no clock, no new firing path; it rides the shim's existing pulse like every probe in the corpus. TRUE when the record shows pulse activations and deactivations whose (served_at - file_mtime) is at most 2 beats, under an unchanged pid.
watchme.enough: 10 add-or-remove events measured within-a-beat with zero loop restarts across them — enough to separate 'discovery serves' from 'the one demo worked'; after that the property is load-bearing and ordinary reds cover regressions.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier
watchme.nexus: the hypothesize tree — the expectation 'presence is service, within one beat, no restart' is the hypothesis each measured event confirms or kills
watchme.consumer: Akien at the gate, and the next voyage that touches the loop (the probe's record is the evidence that discovery held while the corpus changed under it)
